key_claims.claim: Inter- and intraobserver variability for UA, MCA, and UtA Doppler is quantifiable and clinically relevant, though heterogeneity across studies limits derivation of universal thresholds for significant change.
Long-term FETO survivors show respiratory morbidity as the most common sequela, with growth faltering at one year that typically improves with catch-up growth.
UA Doppler-based classification stratifies sFGR severity in MCDA twins but has limited discriminatory performance for predicting adverse outcomes.
A bilateral multisite UA Doppler scoring system correlates with composite adverse perinatal outcome in both early- and late-onset FGR.
Fetuses exposed to threatened preterm labor without intra-amniotic infection demonstrate measurable cardiac remodeling on echocardiography even when delivered at term.
